explanations: luna: The section's stone basin and abundant water find a concrete water-source parallel when striking the rock makes twelve springs gush, with each group knowing its drinking place. | terra: A struck stone releases twelve springs, each people knows its drinking place, and all are told to eat and drink from God's provision: stonework, water turns, and filling meet.
terra: After receiving stone-born springs and divine food, Israel says it cannot endure one food and demands varied produce; appetite rejects the measured gift already filling it.
terra: Stones split and water comes out, while others fall in awe of God; the section's upright well-stones are returned here to their life-giving source and Godward stance.

luna: The section's رغبة is directed toward the Lord; the same root in يَرْغَبُ عَن مِلَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ marks turning away from Abraham's way, the contrary direction. | terra: مَن يَرْغَبُ عَن مِّلَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ uses رغب with عَنْ for aversion, reversing the section's رغب with إِلَىٰ and exposing the importance of desire's direction.
terra: Those who trade away revelation for a small price consume nothing but fire into their bellies, a spiritual boundary on the image of the great eater.
terra: The nursing household's food, clothing, and duty are limited by لَا تُكَلَّفُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا, applying vessel-like capacity to bodily provision and care.
terra: At the river Saul limits drinking to a single handful; measured appetite at water immediately precedes the prayer that God pour patience in 2:250.

luna: The section explains pouring from a bucket as the source of the prayer أفرغ علينا صبرا; here Saul's followers use that exact plea for patience and firm feet before Goliath's forces. | terra: رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا makes patience something poured over Saul's outnumbered company; the following request to steady their feet shows what that filling enables.

luna: The section figures the expanded chest as increased capacity; this verse says God charges no soul beyond its capacity, giving a specific limit to that image. | terra: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا states that obligation is fitted to inner capacity; it explains why enlargement of the breast matters when a burden is borne.
terra: Appetites for family, wealth, livestock, and cultivation are made alluring, but the ayah calls them only the provision of the nearer life.
terra: The answer to worldly appetites in 3:14 is a better gift with their Lord, redirecting desire from transient contents toward its lasting destination.
terra: The command to hasten toward forgiveness and a Garden as wide as the heavens and earth links Godward effort with an expansiveness prepared as reward.
terra: God tests what is in the breasts and purifies what is in the hearts, treating the inner self as a container whose contents can be examined and refined.
terra: Those consuming orphan wealth unjustly eat fire into their bellies, exposing the moral content hidden inside voracious intake.

terra: تَرْغَبُونَ أَن تَنكِحُوهُنَّ uses the رغبة root around orphan women and justice; because the construction permits desire to marry or aversion from marrying, it only tentatively shows appetite being disciplined by another's rights.
terra: Animals sacrificed عَلَى النُّصُبِ make erected stone a site of forbidden devotion, the opposite use from stones forming a water basin.
terra: الْأَنصَابُ are erected cult stones declared defilement; they oppose the source dictionary's erected stones that support a life-giving well.

luna: The section's 94:1 chest is a widened vessel; this verse uses the same root in يشرح صدره for opening the chest to Islam, then contrasts it with a chest made tight and constricted. | terra: God's يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ is set against a breast made ضَيِّقًا حَرَجًا, defining the section's enlarged inner volume by its exact opposite.
terra: Justice in measure and weight is followed by لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا; capacity is a limit to obligation as surely as volume limits a vessel.
terra: فَلَا يَكُن فِي صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ forbids constriction in the Prophet's breast as he receives the Book and warns, the negative boundary of the expanded breast.

luna: The section records the secondary gloss of رغب as gluttony; this command permits eating and drinking but sets a boundary against excess, making appetite's limit explicit. | terra: كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا وَلَا تُسْرِفُوا places an explicit boundary around eating and drinking, correcting the source dictionary's wide-bellied gluttony.
terra: The people of the Garden are introduced with لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا, linking the final abundance with a life whose demands fit human capacity.

luna: The section quotes أفرغ علينا صبرا; here Pharaoh's threatened magicians pray those words for patience and ask to die as Muslims, making the pouring metaphor a plea under threat. | terra: The threatened magicians ask رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا: divine patience is poured into people facing death, exactly the section's bucket metaphor.

luna: This repeated account of twelve springs gushing from a struck rock gives each tribe a known place to drink, matching the section's built water source and provision. | terra: Twelve springs issue from the struck stone and every tribe knows its drinking place, directly staging apportioned water at stone sources.

luna: The section brings water and a heart needing support together; here rain purifies the believers while God strengthens their hearts and steadies their feet. | terra: Water descends from heaven to cleanse, remove inner defilement, bind hearts, and steady feet; it unites poured water with the heart-binding of 28:10 and the steadied feet of 2:250.

luna: The section ends by turning desire toward the Lord and glosses راغب as desire; this verse says إنا إلى الله راغبون while speaking of God's and the Messenger's gifts from bounty. | terra: إِنَّا إِلَى اللَّهِ رَاغِبُونَ closely restates the section's final direction, while God's promised bounty supplies the source dictionary's sense of a great gift one desires.
terra: The earth becomes narrow for the three بِمَا رَحُبَتْ and their own selves constrict; objective spaciousness cannot fill an inwardly closed person.
terra: This ayah unusually gathers both images: thirst, نَصَبٌ, and hunger are endured, while believers are forbidden أَن يَرْغَبُوا بِأَنفُسِهِمْ عَن نَّفْسِهِ, reversing self-directed desire.
terra: وَضَائِقٌ بِهِ صَدْرُكَ names the Prophet's breast tightening under hostile demands, reversing the spaciousness granted for his charge.

luna: The section moves water from a bucket toward a basin; here the floodwater subsides when earth is told to swallow its water and sky to stop, a large-scale reversal in which abundant water disappears. | terra: The earth is ordered to swallow its water and the sky to withhold, until وَغِيضَ الْمَاءُ; the flood-container is emptied under divine command.
terra: The brothers' proposal places Joseph in the hidden depth of a well so that a caravan may recover him, establishing the well scene whose bucket appears in 12:19.
terra: Joseph is actually lowered into the well's depth here; this is the human content later drawn out by the water carrier's bucket in 12:19.

luna: The section's bucket and well scene has a concrete counterpart when a water-drawer lowers his bucket into a well; unexpectedly, it brings up Joseph rather than water, reversing the tool's ordinary purpose. | terra: The water drawer lowers دَلْوَهُ into the well and draws Joseph out, staging the bucket and wellhead that underlie the section's concrete sense of emptying.
terra: One who calls on others is like a person stretching hands toward water that will never reach the mouth; failed drinking becomes a precise reversal of desire directed to the true Lord.
terra: Rain fills valleys بِقَدَرِهَا, each according to its capacity, and the flood bears off foam while useful matter remains; the image tests vessel-size by what it can receive and retain.

luna: The section presents Musa's mother's heart as empty of patience and then bound; this verse says hearts find reassurance in remembering God, a specific account of how an inward state becomes settled.
terra: وَأَفْئِدَتُهُمْ هَوَاءٌ depicts hearts as hollow or vacant, a direct nonlexical counterpart to the heart emptied of patience in 28:10.

terra: All things have their treasuries with God and descend only in a known measure; the ayah supplies a vast source, measured release, and bounded receiving capacity immediately before the water of 15:22.
terra: God sends water down and gives it as drink while humans are not its keepers, وَمَا أَنتُمْ لَهُ بِخَازِنِينَ; the filled store ultimately belongs to the giver.
terra: The Garden's inhabitants are touched by no نَصَبٌ and never expelled; toil is a present command whose final Godward destination has no fatigue.
terra: The Prophet's breast narrows because of what opponents say; 15:98-99 then direct that constrained interior toward praise, prostration, and worship.
terra: When the Prophet's breast is constricted in 15:97, he is told to glorify his Lord and prostrate, answering inner constriction with directed worship.
terra: The command to worship the Lord until certainty comes continues the response to the constricted breast, much as the section ends by directing effort and desire toward the Lord.
terra: مَا عِندَكُمْ يَنفَدُ وَمَا عِندَ اللَّهِ بَاقٍ contrasts what is exhausted with what remains with God, giving the emptied vessel a reason to turn toward its inexhaustible source.

luna: The section's opened chest is a sign of increased capacity; here شرح بالكفر صدرا describes willingly opening the chest to disbelief, the reverse direction from the section's Godward image. | terra: مَن شَرَحَ بِالْكُفْرِ صَدْرًا uses the same opening of the breast for willing unbelief, showing that enlarged capacity is defined also by what one chooses to admit.
terra: A secure town once received abundant provision from every place, then tasted enveloping hunger after ingratitude; fullness becomes emptiness when the gift's source is denied.
terra: The response to the hungry town's example is to eat lawful good provision and thank God, setting gratitude as the boundary of appetite.
terra: وَمَا صَبْرُكَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ states directly that the addressee's patience comes only through God, supplying the agency behind the section's image of patience poured down.

luna: The section's empty heart is held together by God's support; here God says وربطنا على قلوبهم before the youths stand and declare that their Lord is the Lord of the heavens and earth. | terra: وَرَبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ repeats God's act of binding hearts, showing the same divine stabilization that keeps the empty heart in 28:10 from spilling its secret.
luna: The section says direct desire toward your Lord; this command tells the Prophet to stay with people who seek their Lord's face and not let his eyes turn toward worldly adornment.

luna: The section turns toward a plentiful water source; this garden owner fears its water may sink into the earth so deeply that it cannot be recovered, a specific boundary on abundance. | terra: A garden's water can sink so deep that its owner cannot retrieve it, reversing the accessible well and abundant pool of the section.
terra: Moses declares that he will travel until reaching the meeting of the two seas; this supplies the water-destination within which he later names his نَصَب in 18:62.
terra: At the meeting of the seas the fish takes its path into the water, locating the journey-fatigue stated in 18:62 inside a concrete water scene.

terra: Moses says the journey has brought نَصَبًا just after passing the meeting of the two seas; the root's toil sense occurs inside a water-journey rather than the source dictionary's stone-basin sense.

terra: Dhu al-Qarnayn says what his Lord has established for him is better and asks the people to help with strength; divine gift and directed labor initiate the structure that receives poured copper in 18:96.

luna: The section develops فرغ as pouring the contents of a vessel; after setting iron blocks between the two mountain sides, Dhul-Qarnayn says أفرغ عليه قطرا, pouring molten copper over the structure. | terra: أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْرًا is the section's literal emptying sense: molten copper is poured over the heated iron until the structure is consolidated.
terra: The barrier can neither be scaled nor pierced after copper is poured in 18:96; this result shows that emptying the molten contents has made the structure firm.
terra: Even if the sea were ink for the Lord's words, the sea would be exhausted first; the largest visible reservoir still empties before divine abundance does.

luna: The section directs desire toward the Lord; Ibrahim's father uses the same root in أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ عَنْ آلِهَتِي to challenge Ibrahim for turning away from his gods, a specific opposite orientation. | terra: أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ عَنْ آلِهَتِي asks whether Abraham turns away from the idols; the same root with عَنْ marks withdrawal rather than desire toward the Lord.

luna: Moses asks رب اشرح لي صدري; the same chest-expansion image becomes a prayer for capacity before a demanding task. | terra: Moses' prayer رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي asks the Lord to enlarge the inner vessel so it can bear the work and speech that follow.
luna: After asking for his chest to be opened in 20:25, Moses asks that his task be made easy; this next step makes the expanded chest's practical purpose explicit.

luna: The section recalls Moses' mother placing her child in water; this verse makes the container explicit, ordering him placed in a box and cast into the river, which delivers him safely to shore rather than letting him be poured away.
terra: Good provision may be eaten, but appetite must not become excess; the gift that fills can turn destructive when its measure is ignored.

luna: The section directs longing to the Lord and names a desired great gift; this command says the Lord's provision is better and more lasting than the worldly display one might covet. | terra: The Prophet is told not to stretch his eyes toward others' worldly enjoyment because the provision of his Lord is better and more lasting; desire is redirected to its true source.
terra: The prophets call upon God رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا; desire becomes a prayerful orientation to God rather than an appetite left to itself.
terra: يُصَبُّ مِن فَوْقِ رُءُوسِهِمُ الْحَمِيمُ uses literal pouring from above, but the emptied liquid vessel delivers torment rather than patience.
terra: The poured boiling water melts what is inside their bellies, turning the body's interior from a capacity for provision into a site of dissolution.
terra: بِئْرٍ مُّعَطَّلَةٍ is an abandoned well amid destroyed settlements, a water-place whose social use and turns have ceased.

luna: The section's image is water collected in a broad basin; this verse says water is sent down in measure and settled in the earth, while God can also take it away. | terra: Water is sent down بِقَدَرٍ, lodged in the earth, and can be taken away; the ayah joins measured filling, storage, and possible emptying.
terra: No soul is charged beyond its capacity, and a truthful record stands with God; the inner vessel has a divinely known limit.

luna: The section's sequence frees a person from work and redirects attention to God; these people remain attentive to remembrance, prayer, and almsgiving even while trade and business could distract them.

terra: Clouds are driven together, joined, and made into a mass before rain emerges through them; gathered abundance empties through an outlet like the source dictionary's collected water and bucket-mouth.
terra: God sends winds before His mercy and sends pure water from the sky, identifying the giver behind the descending supply.
terra: The water revives dead land and gives drink to cattle and many people, showing what the poured provision fills and restores.
terra: Moses fears rejection and says وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي, a mission-bearing chest constricted where his later prayer asks that it be expanded.
terra: Abraham identifies the Lord as the one who feeds and gives drink, joining the filling of hunger and thirst to proper Godward dependence.
terra: The she-camel has one drinking share and the people another on an appointed day, giving the section's wellside image a literal water-turn.

luna: The section uses 28:10's empty heart after Moses' mother parts from her child; this earlier verse supplies the act behind that state, telling her to nurse him and cast him into the river if she fears for him. | terra: Moses' mother is told to cast him into the river and trust the promise of his return; this supplies the water-separation that leaves her heart empty in 28:10.

luna: The section explicitly reads فؤاد أم موسى فارغا as an empty vessel, empty of patience after she puts her child in the water; the verse says God had to bind her heart to keep her steady. | terra: The section explicitly develops فَارِغًا here: Moses' mother's heart is an emptied vessel, while God's binding of it keeps that emptied heart from disclosing her secret.
terra: Moses is restored to his mother so her eye may be cooled and she need not grieve, completing the divine refilling and reassurance of the emptied heart in 28:10.

luna: The section's wellhead image is echoed by the water point at Midian, where people water their flocks and two women hold theirs back; 28:24 completes the scene with Moses watering for them. | terra: At Midian's water Moses finds a whole community watering and two women held back; the well is a place of ordered access and turns, as in the section's water-round.

luna: The section pictures turning toward abundant water; in the Midian well scene set at 28:23, Moses draws water for the two women, making the source a concrete provision for those waiting there. | terra: Moses waters for the women, then turns to his Lord as one in need of any good sent down; watering is followed immediately by Godward desire for provision.

terra: After Moses waters and petitions his Lord in 28:24, one woman brings an invitation to recompense him for that watering; needed provision arrives through the very act of emptying water for others.

terra: نَصِيبَكَ here means one's allotted share, while the ayah directs God's gift toward seeking the Hereafter; the source dictionary's homonymous نَصِيب, a stone basin, makes portion and receptacle meet.
terra: “My earth is spacious, so worship Me” joins width with an exclusive Godward command, paralleling the widened interior's final orientation to its Lord.
terra: God raises clouds, spreads and fragments them, and rain comes from within them; the gathered container releases its provision and its recipients rejoice.
terra: A sea replenished by seven more seas cannot exhaust God's words, expanding the section's wide reservoir image beyond every finite capacity.

luna: The section's bucket and basin sequence includes pouring liquid; this verse says a spring of molten copper was made to flow for Solomon, and 34:13 continues with enormous basins and fixed pots. | terra: God makes a flowing spring of molten copper, عَيْنَ الْقِطْرِ, turning the same material poured in 18:96 into a water-source image beside the huge vessels of 34:13.

luna: The section names a spacious basin as part of its water image; this verse depicts جِفَانٍ كَالْجَوَابِ, huge basins like reservoirs, alongside fixed cooking pots. The preceding 34:12 supplies the flowing copper source. | terra: جِفَانٍ كَالْجَوَابِ are great basins like reservoirs, the Quran's closest concrete counterpart to the section's wide hollow basin.
terra: Whatever believers spend, God replaces; what is poured out in faithful use is answered by the Provider rather than guarded as a permanently full private vessel.
terra: In the lasting abode, لَا يَمَسُّنَا فِيهَا نَصَبٌ; the laboring sense of the root ends where divine bounty does not run out.
terra: Gardens of palms and grapes have springs made to gush within them, making abundant water the interior source of fruit and provision.
terra: A cup from a flowing spring is passed among the blessed, pairing a bounded drinking vessel with abundant source-water.
terra: The people of Hell fill their bellies from the tree of Zaqqūm, a horrifying realization of the section's large belly rather than a desirable great gift.
terra: After their bellies are filled, they receive a mixture of boiling water, joining unchecked appetite to a punishing drink.
terra: Job names his affliction نُصْبٍ وَعَذَابٍ; the root's toil sense is immediately answered in 38:42 by a water source for washing and drinking.
terra: After the نُصْب of 38:41, Job strikes the ground and receives a cool bath and drink, bringing exertion to a restorative water-place.

luna: The section develops a well and abundant gathered water; this verse traces water through the earth as springs, then shows the growth it sustains before the plants dry and break apart. | terra: Rain is threaded into springs in the earth, raises vegetation, and leaves it dry debris; a stored water-source fills living forms and then visibly runs out.

luna: The section begins with an expanded chest; this verse repeats شرح الصدر for a chest opened to Islam and sets it against hearts hardened at God's remembrance. | terra: أَفَمَن شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ repeats the expanded breast and states what fills that new capacity: Islam and light from one's Lord.
terra: The angels pray that their Lord encompasses all things in mercy and knowledge; divine vastness becomes the ground for asking that repentant people be admitted and filled with mercy.

terra: One who desires the Hereafter's harvest receives increase, while one who desires the world's gets some of it but no نَصِيب in the Hereafter; appetite is defined by its chosen destination and share.
terra: If God expanded provision without measure people would transgress, so He sends it down in the amount He wills; the wide vessel and large gift require a governing limit.
terra: Whatever people are given is temporary enjoyment, while what is with God is better and more lasting for those who rely on their Lord; desire is redirected from finite contents to their source.
terra: Golden platters and cups circulate while the Garden contains مَا تَشْتَهِيهِ الْأَنفُسُ; vessels and appetite meet in a gift that truly answers desire.
terra: Zaqqūm is like molten substance inside the bellies, bringing the section's poured metal and wide interior together as punishment.
terra: The molten food boils in bellies like scalding water, turning both vessel and liquid against the eater.
terra: ثُمَّ صُبُّوا فَوْقَ رَأْسِهِ مِنْ عَذَابِ الْحَمِيمِ reverses patience poured over believers: boiling punishment is poured over the condemned.

luna: The section's secondary image is a wide-bellied, voracious eater; this verse depicts disbelievers eating as livestock eat and contrasts that immediate appetite with the Fire as their destination. | terra: Those who merely enjoy themselves and eat كَمَا تَأْكُلُ الْأَنْعَامُ embody the ungoverned, wide-bellied appetite named in the source dictionary.
terra: The promised Garden contains rivers of unspoiled water, milk, wine, and honey, extending the wide basin into an abundance whose contents do not spoil.

luna: The section makes the heart a receptacle that can be empty of patience; here God sends tranquility into believers' hearts and increases their faith, an inward filling with steadiness. | terra: God sends tranquility down into believers' hearts so that faith increases, a positive inner filling comparable to patience poured into a heart emptied by fear.
terra: A human being has only what he strives for, supplying the effort that reaches its explicit endpoint with the Lord in 53:42.
terra: وَأَنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ الْمُنتَهَىٰ names the Lord as the terminus of the striving stated in 53:39, closely matching the sequence of labor followed by Godward direction.
terra: The gates of heaven open بِمَاءٍ مُّنْهَمِرٍ, a torrent poured down before waters gather in 54:12.
terra: Springs burst from the earth and the two waters meet عَلَىٰ أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ, combining gathered abundance with exact measure.
terra: الْمَاءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ makes water an apportioned turn, with each drink attended in sequence.
terra: The people call their companion and he hamstrings the she-camel, violently breaking the apportioned water arrangement announced in 54:28.

luna: The section glosses فراغ as the opposite of occupation; the different use سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ promises that God will attend to the two groups, reversing the direction of attention in the section's human turning toward God. | terra: The source defines farāgh first as the opposite of occupation; سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ uses that root idiomatically for God's concentrated reckoning, a consequential sense distinct from pouring out a vessel.
luna: The section shows molten copper poured over an iron structure to strengthen it; here molten copper is sent upon the two as a punishment, reversing the material's role.

luna: The section's water vessel and source meet in this cup scene: cups, ewers, and a drink from a flowing spring are served to the people of the Garden. | terra: Cups, ewers, and a cup from a flowing spring combine portable vessels with an unconfined water source.
terra: فَمَالِئُونَ مِنْهَا الْبُطُونَ makes belly-filling explicit, but the contents are Zaqqūm rather than the bountiful gift desire seeks.
terra: The filled bellies are followed by drinking boiling water, joining appetite and water in a ruined feast.
terra: They drink like desperately thirsty camels, an image of appetite that cannot find its measure even while being filled.

luna: The section turns toward a plentiful water source; this verse asks about the water people drink, while 56:69 names its descent and 56:70 the possibility of its becoming undrinkable. | terra: The question أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ الْمَاءَ الَّذِي تَشْرَبُونَ turns attention from the drinker's appetite to the water itself.

luna: The section joins a water source to desire for the Lord; this verse asks whether people send down their drinking water or God does, and 56:70 supplies the boundary that God could make it bitter. | terra: The next question asks whether people sent water from the cloud or God did, identifying the true provider at the far end of the vessel.

luna: The section's wide basin and desired water signify abundance; this verse says God could make drinking water bitter, completing the preceding question about who sends it down. | terra: God could make the drinking water bitter; the desired filling of the vessel is therefore a gift rather than an entitlement.
terra: Believers are told to race toward forgiveness and a Garden as wide as heaven and earth, explicitly identifying that vast capacity as God's bounty.
luna: The section reads فرغت as becoming free of an occupation and then turning toward God; this verse begins فَإِذَا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلَاةُ, then sends people out to seek God's bounty.
terra: Spending is scaled to what one has been given, and God promises ease after constraint; provision, capacity, and what may be poured out are held in one measure.

luna: The section's well, bucket, and gathered water meet a clear boundary here: if water sinks into the earth, who can bring accessible running water? The question turns dependence toward God. | terra: If the community's water sinks away, no one else can bring flowing water; the full basin is bounded by the giver's power to leave it empty.

luna: The section names gluttonous appetite and a much-desired gift; in the garden parable, the owners plan to exclude the poor from the crop, and 68:31-32 completes the scene with their remorse and renewed hope in their Lord.

luna: The section joins desire toward the Lord to a great gift one longs for; after the garden owners lose their hoarded crop, they say إنا إلى ربنا راغبون and hope their Lord will replace it with something better.
terra: People rush from graves كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ, as if racing toward a raised marker; the destination reverses the command to direct desire toward the Lord.

luna: The section turns its desire toward the Lord; Noah tells his people to seek forgiveness from their Lord, and 71:11-12 completes the appeal with promised rain, gardens, rivers, wealth, and children.

luna: The section's gathered water and desired abundance meet the promise يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا, abundant rain after the appeal to seek the Lord in 71:10; 71:12 adds gardens and rivers. | terra: Noah promises that turning to God will bring the sky's water in abundance, making abundant outpouring a gift sought from its Lord.

luna: The section links the Lordward desire to a great gift and abundant water; this verse promises wealth, children, gardens, and rivers, completing the rain promise in 71:11. | terra: The abundant rain of 71:11 continues as wealth, children, gardens, and rivers, spelling out the large desirable gift that fills more than bodily thirst.
luna: The section's spacious basin holds abundant water toward which one turns; this verse promises that a people who remain on the right path will be given مَاءً غَدَقًا, abundant water.
luna: The section's abundant water is a desired provision; the next verse says it is also a test and warns whoever turns from remembrance of his Lord, giving a boundary to the promise in 72:16.

luna: The section's فراغ is the opposite of being occupied; this verse names the Prophet's سَبْحًا طَوِيلًا, a long daytime occupation, and 73:8 completes the movement by commanding devotion to his Lord.

luna: The section moves from finishing to turning desire toward the Lord; this command to remember the Lord and وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا gives that Godward devotion, while 73:7 names the long daytime occupation.
luna: The section's closing movement is to turn toward one's Lord after exertion; this command to the Prophet says to be patient for his Lord, joining effort, patience, and Lordward orientation.

luna: The section moves between bucket, basin, and water source; this verse describes a spring from which God's servants drink and which they make gush abundantly. | terra: The righteous drink from a spring which God's servants cause to flow abundantly, joining a drinking vessel's source to deliberate distribution of its water.
terra: Silver vessels and crystal cups are passed around the blessed, placing the container itself inside the scene of abundant provision.
terra: The crystal vessels are قَدَّرُوهَا تَقْدِيرًا, measured to their proper amount; volume and provision are fitted to one another rather than appetite being limitless.
terra: Salsabīl is the named spring behind the Garden's drink, continuing the section's movement from measured cups to an abundant water source.
terra: وَسَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَرَابًا طَهُورًا explicitly joins the Lord with the giving of drink, making concrete the section's movement toward the source of gathered water.
terra: Lofty mountains and sweet water are placed together, a concise Quranic meeting of erected stone mass and life-giving drink.
luna: The section develops water being poured from a vessel and abundant water as provision; this verse describes copious rain pouring down, and 78:15 gives the resulting grain and plants.
terra: وَكَأْسًا دِهَاقًا presents a cup filled to abundance, the positive completion of an emptied container.
luna: The section glosses رغِيبة as a great gift one would desire; this verse calls the reward from the Lord a measured and ample gift, a specific divine-gift counterpart.

luna: The section glosses emptying a bucket as pouring out what it contains; this verse depicts water poured down in abundance, with 80:26-32 continuing through crops and food as its provision. | terra: أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا الْمَاءَ صَبًّا uses the very verb with which the source dictionary explains emptying a bucket, but makes God the giver who pours water for food.
terra: The graves are scattered open, a further image of closed earthly containers discharging what was held inside them.
terra: Tasnim is identified as a spring from which those brought near drink, again placing a privileged drink in relation to its source rather than the cup alone.
terra: The earth is first stretched out in وَإِذَا الْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ; this enlarged container is the one that empties itself in 84:4.

luna: The section's chest and bucket are images of a container emptied of what it holds; this verse says the earth casts out what is within it and empties itself, extending that action to the earth. | terra: وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ gives the fullest nonlexical parallel: the earth casts out its contents and becomes empty like a discharged vessel.
terra: After emptying in 84:4, the earth hearkens to its Lord; that sequence parallels the section's emptied vessel followed by orientation to the Lord.
terra: The human being labors toward the Lord and will meet Him, closely joining the section's فَانصَبْ with وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ even without its vessel words.
terra: The condemned are given drink from a boiling spring, reversing both the desired water source and the restorative drink of the section's wellside scene.
terra: A running spring supplies the water-side of the Garden scene whose cups are set out in 88:14.
terra: وَأَكْوَابٌ مَّوْضُوعَةٌ places ready vessels beside the running spring of 88:12, a peaceful counterpart to the section's well and basin.
terra: وَإِلَى الْجِبَالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ uses the root for massive stones set upright, clarifying the physical act behind the source dictionary's basin built from erected stones.
terra: فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذَابٍ retains both pouring and your Lord but makes the poured content punishment, the sharp inverse of poured patience and desired bounty.
terra: Devouring inheritance with an all-consuming appetite gives a social form to the source dictionary's wide-bellied gluttony.
terra: Intense love of wealth follows voracious consumption in 89:19, showing desire expanding beyond bodily capacity into acquisitiveness.
terra: God's messenger identifies both God's she-camel and her watering right, a compact parallel to the section's ordered turn at the communal water source.
terra: The people deny the messenger and hamstring the she-camel, rejecting the watering boundary stated in 91:13 and bringing judgment from their Lord.
luna: The section's dictionary note calls a رغِيبة a great desired gift; here the Lord promises to give the Prophet until he is satisfied, a concrete instance of generous divine giving.

luna: The section describes a vessel emptied of its contents; this repeated earth image says the earth brings out its burdens, a specific parallel of concealed contents being released. | terra: وَأَخْرَجَتِ الْأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا makes the earth discharge its burdens like a container emptied of what weighed inside it.

luna: The section connects appetite with a great desired gift; this verse says the human being is intense in love of wealth, and the same short passage proceeds to what is exposed in the chests at 100:10.

luna: The section's vessel image brings hidden contents into view; this verse supplies the resurrection setting, when what lies in graves is scattered, before 100:10 names what is exposed in chests. | terra: The graves are overturned and their contents raised before the breasts' contents are exposed in 100:10, enlarging the emptying scene beyond the chest alone.

luna: The section treats the chest as a vessel whose contents are brought out; this verse says what is in the chests is exposed, a direct inner-content parallel. | terra: The section cites وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِي الصُّدُورِ as the contents of breast-vessels being brought out and exposed.
luna: After the section's image of chest contents exposed at 100:10, this closing verse adds that their Lord is fully aware of them on that day, completing the disclosure with its divine witness.
terra: The command فَلْيَعْبُدُوا رَبَّ هَٰذَا الْبَيْتِ directs response to the Lord, and 106:4 identifies Him as the one who fills hunger and secures fear.
terra: Feeding مِن جُوعٍ makes the Lord's provision the answer to the empty, hungry belly developed in the section.
terra: إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ الْكَوْثَرَ is an overflowing grant of abundance, closely matching the source dictionary's رغِيبة, a great gift desired.
terra: The abundant gift in 108:1 is followed by فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ, the same movement from received bounty to action directed exclusively to one's Lord.
